entries.name: Case serial between the lugs at 6 o'clock
entries.looks_like: A number engraved across the case between the two lower lugs, on the 6 o'clock side, hidden by the bracelet or strap: digits only to 1987 (up to seven), then a letter and six digits (R123456) to about 2010.
entries.means: The case's serial number; dates the case by the Rolex serial table (rolex.json). Not the model reference, which is at 12 o'clock.
entries.date_note: Between the lugs until about 2008; from about 2005 also on the rehaut, and from about 2008 only there. When this location began is not settled by the sources.

visual.method: The position is fixed by sources bobs-rolex-serials and rolex-date-chart-pdf: between the lugs on the 6 o'clock side, drawn as the case edge and the two lugs seen from below. The digit style is illustrative: example serial 5398992 (a dated watch in rolex.json, warranty card 1979) set in a plain sans-serif (Helvetica regular), ink on paper, 4x supersampled (hallmark-sources/draw_watch_numbers.py). Drawn from the description, not traced.
visual.credit: Drawn by Heirloom from the published descriptions; not a photograph.

entries.name: Model reference between the lugs at 12 o'clock
entries.looks_like: A four- to six-digit number engraved between the two upper lugs, on the 12 o'clock side, hidden by the bracelet; on older watches often stamped inside the case back as well.
entries.means: The model reference: it names the model, bezel and metal (a Datejust 16234, a Submariner 5513) and is shared by every watch of that model. It is not a serial and does not date the watch.

sources.where: 'Ref.' and 'inside case back stamped' in lot descriptions

visual.method: The position is fixed by sources bobs-rolex-serials and swisswatchexpo-rolex-serials: between the lugs on the 12 o'clock side, drawn as the case edge and the two lugs. The digit style is illustrative: example reference 5513 (a Submariner reference among the dated watches in rolex.json) set in a plain sans-serif (Helvetica regular), ink on paper, 4x supersampled (hallmark-sources/draw_watch_numbers.py). Drawn from the description, not traced.
visual.credit: Drawn by Heirloom from the published descriptions; not a photograph.

entries.name: Case serial on the rehaut at 6 o'clock
entries.looks_like: The serial engraved in the inner ring between the dial and the crystal (the rehaut), at 6 o'clock, in the gap in the repeated ROLEX engraving; readable through the crystal.
entries.means: The same case serial, moved where it can be read without removing the bracelet. Random serials (from about 2010) carry no date.
entries.date_note: Also between the lugs from about 2005 to 2008, then only on the rehaut.

disagreements.note: BeckerTime puts the start in 2006-2007 on some models; Bob's and the date chart give 2005.

searched: Wikimedia Commons: Category:Rolex watches and Category:Omega watches with subcategories to depth 3, and full-text searches (2026-11-22)
Commons: Rolex Datejust 36 and Datejust 126234 photographs by ajay_suresh (CC BY 2.0): the rehaut is visible but a reflection covers the serial at 6 o'clock
visual.note: The two Commons photos that show a rehaut have the serial hidden by a reflection.

entries.name: ROLEX engraved round the rehaut
entries.looks_like: The word ROLEX repeated in small capitals all the way round the inner ring between the dial and the crystal, with a gap at 6 o'clock for the serial and a small coronet at 12.
entries.means: A Rolex trademark engraving added to the rehaut; it marks a case of about 2004-2005 or later.
entries.date_note: 2004 (Turn-O-Graph first) or 2005 (Datejust first): the sources disagree.

searched: Wikimedia Commons: Category:Rolex watches and Category:Omega watches with subcategories to depth 3, and full-text searches (2026-11-22)

Commons: Rolex Datejust 36 (ajay_suresh, CC BY 2.0) shows the engraving, but its letters are about 25 px tall; its letters are about 25 px on a curve, and any crop of 90 px or more takes in the minute track
visual.note: Usable source photo exists at too low a resolution for a single-mark crop.

entries.name: Rolex coronet
entries.looks_like: A five-pointed crown, each point ending in a small ball, above an oval base; applied in metal on the dial at 12 o'clock, and embossed on the winding crown.
entries.means: Rolex's trademark. It names the maker; it does not date the watch or show that it is genuine.
entries.date_note: Registered as a trademark in 1925 (Britannica) or 1931 (Swiss Watch Expo); on dials from the 1930s and on winding crowns from the 1950s.

visual.credit: Photograph: "Rolex Datejust 36 - Black Sunburst Dial" by ajay_suresh, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0; cropped and toned by Heirloom.
visual.note: The applied coronet on a recent Datejust dial.

entries.name: ROLEX on the dial
entries.looks_like: The word ROLEX in serif capitals below the coronet at 12 o'clock, usually followed by the model name (OYSTER PERPETUAL, DATEJUST).
entries.means: The maker's name, registered as a trademark by Hans Wilsdorf in 1908. It names the maker; it does not date the watch or show that it is genuine.

visual.credit: Photograph: "Rolex Datejust 36 - Black Sunburst Dial" by ajay_suresh, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0; cropped and toned by Heirloom.
visual.note: ROLEX on a recent Datejust dial, cut at the photo's native resolution.

entries.name: Movement serial number
entries.looks_like: Seven or eight digits engraved on a plate or bridge of the movement, seen with the case back off (for example 13977738).
entries.means: The movement's serial number; dates the movement to about a year or two by the Omega serial table (omega.json), from 1,000,000 (about 1894) to about 56,000,000 (about 1995).
entries.date_note: On the movement through most of the 20th century; from about 1991 also on the case back or a lug.

entries.name: Caliber number on the movement
entries.looks_like: A short number, usually three digits, engraved on the movement beside the Omega sign (Ω 266, 321, 565).
entries.means: The movement's model (caliber), shared by every movement of that design. It is not a serial and does not date the watch; a caliber's production years narrow it.

entries.name: OMEGA on the movement
entries.looks_like: The word OMEGA in capitals engraved on a bridge of the movement, often with SWISS and the jewel count (17 JEWELS).
entries.means: The maker's name. Omega was the name of the Brandt brothers' 1894 caliber; Louis Brandt & Frère took it as the company name in 1903.
entries.date_note: The name dates from the 1894 caliber; the company used it from 1903.

entries.name: Serial on the case back or a lug
entries.looks_like: An eight-digit number engraved on the outside of the case back or on the side of a lug.
entries.means: The watch's serial, engraved where it can be read without opening the case. From about 1995 numbers were given in blocks by caliber, so it does not date the watch by itself.
entries.date_note: From 15 February 1991 per Brittons (citing Richon); 'the early 1990s' per Bob's.

entries.name: Model reference inside the case back
entries.looks_like: A reference stamped inside the case back, in forms such as 2915-1, 165.024 or ST 145.022-69; later watches use longer product codes with dots (311.30.42.30.01.005).
entries.means: The model reference, shared by every watch of that model. It is not a serial and does not date the watch.
